name: High-Luminosity LHC
notes: Sources disagree on the start date: home.cern/science/accelerators/hilumi-lhc says the HiLumi LHC 'should be operational in mid-2030' and src:cern-ls3-farewell-2026 says it is 'scheduled to begin operation in 2030', while ATLAS's own upgrade feature says Run 4 is 'currently planned for 2029'. 2030 is recorded here (two CERN accelerator-side sources); the 2029 date is recorded on experiment:atlas, which is what that ATLAS page describes.

circumference.note: HL-LHC reuses the LHC ring; ~1.2 km of it is replaced.

summary.plain: A major upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider now being installed. By replacing about 1.2 kilometres of the ring with new magnets and equipment it will squeeze the beams harder so that many more collisions happen each second, giving the experiments roughly ten times more data.
summary.technical: Luminosity upgrade of accelerator:lhc: new Nb3Sn inner triplets, crab cavities, superconducting links and collimation over ~1.2 km, targeting a factor-10 increase in integrated luminosity over the LHC design value; installed during LS3 and scheduled to begin operation in 2030.
